droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `permission_revoke` (permission_revoke): Grant a permission through the app, revoke it the way Settings does, come back and use the feature again.
Steps: [{"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"accept_permission": true}, {"settle": 3}, {"fault": "revoke_permission", "permission": "android.permission.CAMERA"}, {"restart_to_screen": true}, {"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"settle": 4.0}]
Result: crashed: java.lang.SecurityException: validateClientPermissionsLocked:1848: Caller "com.shubhasai.monkeymart" (PID 6283, UID 10234) cannot open camera "1" without camera permission
Crash: java.lang.SecurityException @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)

## Rules

content.text:
The crash came from a stale `camera_granted` flag in SharedPreferences, set when the permission was first granted. After the permission was revoked in Settings, the flag still said "granted", so the app called `openCamera` without it and hit the `SecurityException`. In `CouponScanner.kt` I removed the flag and now check the real permission each time with `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission`. The tap handler goes through a new `CouponScanner.onScanClicked`, which re-requests the permission when it's missing. I haven't compiled or run any tests.

The regression test is `CouponScannerPermissionTest`, and it only exercises that `onScanClicked` decision logic. It does not run the real permission check, since a plain JVM test can't build an Android `Context` without Mockito or Robolectric. It fails against the old code because `onScanClicked` doesn't exist there, so that failure is a compile error rather than a behaviour failure.
